subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should a silent memory-triggered compaction run be allowed to write non-memory workspace files through the normal write tool guard, or must it remain restricted to the single daily memory target?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes the write boundary for a silent runtime event; automation should not choose that security/product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
options.body: Delegate paths outside the memory directory to the existing write tool while keeping memory-file writes restricted to the configured append-only target, with focused tests and docs.

options.title: Keep strict memory-only writes
options.body: Preserve the current single-target guard and document that normal file edits must wait for or disable memory flush during compaction.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the default strict and add an operator-controlled setting or command only if maintainers accept the extra config surface.

recommendation.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Delegate paths outside the memory directory to the existing write tool while keeping memory-file writes restricted to the configured append-only target, with focused tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strict guard and write-path forwarding history points to this owner as the closest implementation route for the security-boundary decision.
